The two decision records and `batch-queue/tasks/i203a.md` had nothing between the path and that colon, so no range or id was found. I confirmed the ids and line ranges I cite against the files, except `outcome.json` lines 1788-1800 and the end of `phase-coding.spec.md`'s PHC-B19, which I took from earlier greps. Every id the hand-off cites resolves to one definition.

**Reading list.**
- It is now one file per item, because the check only tests the first file named in an item.
- No range contains a colon.
- Items that had no range now have one: the two decision records `(lines 14-22 and 32-34)` / `(lines 14-22 and 36-38)`, the task `(lines 9-40)` and the commands file `(lines 1-12)`.

- G3 now names the documents that close it, plus what `upgrade-check --stamp` writes and which engine modules the stamp reads.
